transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before we finalize the authentication-library patch rollout, I want to make sure we've covered all our bases. The patch has passed our lab tests and the current draft proposes a Thursday 02:00 UTC canary for 60 minutes with broad deployment on Friday. As the decision-maker on this rollout, I need us to complete the required final round-robin check with application platform, reliability, and compliance before I can approve the plan. Can we go through those sign-offs now?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. While debugging an unrelated authentication test this morning, I confirmed that the Ledger service uses a custom fork of the authentication library. Ledger must have the compatibility flag enabled before broad deployment, and it must be excluded from the canary until that flag is enabled. I haven't updated the rollout document yet because the compatibility test completed only minutes ago, but this needs to be factored into the plan before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical staffing issue for the reliability sign-off. While preparing another maintenance window, I checked the current on-call rota and confirmed that I am the only engineer qualified to perform rollback for this patch during Wednesday 18:00-22:00 UTC. More importantly, the Thursday 02:00 UTC canary slot has no qualified rollback engineer at all. I haven't posted the staffing confirmation yet because the rota change is still being recorded, but this directly affects the proposed canary window — we cannot proceed with a Thursday 02:00 UTC canary unless we have a qualified rollback engineer on call.
